comparators.base_form: Minsky (1967) two-counter machine with INC/DEC and zero-test branches, as a one-way deterministic acceptor
comparators.parameter_mapping: card q -> finite control state; card c1, c2 -> counters 1, 2; card delta -> machine program; card y_t -> acceptance at halt
comparators.read: y_t = 1[q_t = c and c1_t = 0 and c2_t = 0]
comparators.update: (q_t, c1_t, c2_t) = delta(q_{t-1}, c1_{t-1}, c2_{t-1}, x_t). a in phase a: c1+=1. b in phase a/b with c1>0: c1-=1, c2+=1, q=b. c in phase b/c with c1=0 and c2>0: c2-=1, q=c. Otherwise q=dead with counters fixed.

comparators.base_form: Input-dependent linear recurrence h_t = A(x_t) h_{t-1}, y_t = C h_t (SSM family form with non-diagonal input-dependent A_t)
comparators.parameter_mapping: card delta(., x) -> 0/1 transition matrix M(x) for x in {a,b,c}; card acceptance predicate -> linear read vector C indicating configuration (c,0,0); card initial (0,0,a) -> h_0 = e_(a,0,0)

transformations.what: Replace the integer counters and phase with a one-hot vector over all reachable configurations (dimension 4(n+1)^2 + 1, growing with n). Every zero-tested branch then becomes a fixed linear transition chosen by the input token.

comparators.update: h_t = M(x_t) h_{t-1}, h_0 = e_(a,0,0). Here h is one-hot over {a,b,c} x [0,n]^2 plus {dead}, and M(x) e_(q,c1,c2) = e_delta(q,c1,c2,x), with e_dead fixed by every M(x).

comparators.base_form: Input-conditioned affine update on the card's own counter coordinates without state tests (the card's named closest comparator)
comparators.parameter_mapping: card c1, c2 -> affine state coordinates; card phase q and zero tests have no image (expected to fail the 0/1/2 zero-test witness and the aabbbcc rejection)
comparators.read: y_t = w0 + w1 c1_t + w2 c2_t

difference_if_any: In native coordinates nothing differs from Minsky's construction; the card states this itself. Against the lifted linear recurrence, the remaining difference is efficiency only. The counter machine keeps O(log n) bits. The one-hot lift needs an O(n^2)-dimensional state, an exponential blow-up in state bits, and its transition matrix family must be defined uniformly as n grows (a shift operator with a zero boundary). Against the blind affine update on the same coordinates (c1 += [x=a] - [x=b], c2 += [x=b] - [x=c]), the difference is real. The state-tested branch to dead, and the indicator read, cannot be written affinely in (c1, c2). This is the card's stated 0/1/2 second-difference witness. No learning rule exists: the program is supplied.
family_why: Under a lifted_state repair (a one-hot state over reachable (q, c1, c2) configurations, growing with n), each token applies a fixed input-selected 0/1 matrix, h_t = M(x_t) h_{t-1}, and the read is linear, y_t = C h_t. That is the ssm form with input-dependent A_t. In native O(log n) coordinates it is a counter machine and outside every listed family.
mapping: Identity mapping onto the Minsky (1967, ch. 14) two-counter machine used as a one-way deterministic acceptor. The card's (q, c1, c2) is the machine's finite control and two counters. The card's delta is the machine's program: INC c1 on 'a' in phase a; on 'b', test c1>0, then DEC c1 and INC c2; on 'c', test c1=0 and c2>0, then DEC c2; every other case goes to an absorbing reject state. The card's y_t = 1[q=c, c1=0, c2=0] is the halting acceptance condition. Adversarial lift into an out-of-scope family: index a one-hot vector h_t by the reachable configurations (q, c1, c2), with c1, c2 in [0, n] plus a dead state. Each delta(., x) is then a fixed 0/1 transition matrix M(x) that moves e_(q,c1,c2) to e_delta(q,c1,c2,x). Every zero test is absorbed into which basis vectors M(x) sends to e_dead. So h_t = M(x_t) h_{t-1}, with h_0 = e_(a,0,0) and y_t = C h_t, where C is the indicator of (c,0,0). This is an input-dependent linear recurrence (SSM form with A_t = M(x_t), B_t = 0, C_t = C). It is exact for every input of length at most n, and the state dimension is 4(n+1)^2 + 1, which grows with n.

comparisons.reference: Minsky (1967), Computation: Finite and Infinite Machines, ch. 14

comparisons.comparator: one-hot lifted input-dependent linear recurrence h_t = M(x_t) h_{t-1}, y_t = C h_t
comparisons.reference: input-dependent linear recurrence (SSM form); one-hot configuration lift of a counter automaton

comparisons.comparator: sanity: card final acceptance vs toy answer key (aabbcc, aabbbcc)
sanity: best affine fit to zero-test outputs 1,0,0 on counter 0,1,2

reduction_check.notes: Outputs are 0/1 acceptance indicators per prefix, no rescaling. Lifted state uses dimension 3(N+1)^2+1 = 508 ({a,b,c}x[0,N]^2 plus dead, as in the declared update; the mapping text says 4(N+1)^2+1), N=12. M(x) is built from the card delta. Blind affine read weights are fixed a priori, not fitted.

textbook_why: This is Minsky's two-counter machine with zero tests (Computation: Finite and Infinite Machines, ch. 14), run as a one-way acceptor on the token stream with an acceptance indicator as readout. The equations change nothing in the construction. Only a specific program (the equal-blocks recognizer) is fixed.
why: The card is explicitly a prior-art diagnostic: a textbook two-counter machine recognizing a^n b^n c^n-type equal blocks. It claims no novelty, and its update and read coincide symbol for symbol with Minsky's counter-machine program. Being adversarial, it also falls into the ssm form under a lifted_state repair the policy allows. A one-hot state over reachable configurations turns every zero test into a fixed input-selected transition matrix, giving h_t = M(x_t) h_{t-1} with a linear read. That lift is exact at all finite lengths, but its state grows as O(n^2) rather than O(log n). The separation the card does establish is only against the same-coordinate, input-conditioned affine update, which the card itself labels as not a proof against state lifts. A 1960s automaton applied to a token stream would not surprise anyone who knows counter automata or RNN-computability results (Siegelmann-Sontag). No outcome-store history matches this card.
